UNH.rationale: UNH presents a mixed but slightly positive picture. The company just reported a strong Q2 2026 beat (adjusted EPS $6.38 vs $4.90 consensus) and raised full-year guidance to $19.50-$20.00 adjusted EPS, with MCR improving to 86.7% from 89.4% YoY. Operating cash flow of $11.1B in Q2 was 1.9x net income, demonstrating strong cash generation. However, several structural concerns temper enthusiasm: (1) membership is declining across segments — UnitedHealthcare served 48.5M consumers, down 525K sequentially, with Medicare Advantage seniors contracting by 965K since year-end 2025; (2) commercial medical cost trends remain 'stubbornly above 11%' with margin recovery pushed past 2027; (3) the DOJ antitrust investigation targeting the vertically integrated model poses a material structural risk; (4) the stock is trading at PE ~30x, near the top of its 365-day range (9.5-31.0), having rallied ~20% in the past quarter. The Q2 beat and guidance raise provide a near-term positive catalyst, but the elevated valuation, shrinking membership base, and regulatory overhang limit upside. The score reflects solid near-term execution offset by rich valuation and meaningful structural headwinds.
key_factors: Q2 2026 adjusted EPS of $6.38 beat consensus of $4.90; full-year guidance raised to $19.50-$20.00
MCR improved to 86.7% from 89.4% YoY, reflecting better pricing and medical management

Commercial medical cost trends 'stubbornly above 11%' with margin recovery pushed past 2027
DOJ antitrust investigation targeting vertical integration between UnitedHealthcare and Optum
PE of ~30x near top of 365-day range (9.5-31.0); stock up ~20% in past quarter
Strong cash generation: Q2 operating cash flow of $11.1B, 1.9x net income

Updated Full Year 2026 Earnings Outlook Range to $18.45 to $18.95 Per Share; Adjusted Earnings Range of $19.50 to $20.00 Per Share
UnitedHealthcare served 48.5 million consumers, down 525,000 sequentially. Seniors served through Medicare Advantage have contracted by 965,000 since year-end 2025
Cash flows from operations were $11.1 billion, or 1.9 times net income
